Tokyo: five nights near Kuramae, which is quieter than Shinjuku and close to the Sumida river for morning runs. Kanazawa: we booked the ryokan Yamanoo for 9 to 11 April 2027, two nights, with a vegetarian kaiseki dinner arranged in advance. From Kanazawa we go to Kyoto on the Thunderbird and Shinkansen connection, about two and a half hours. Kyoto: four nights in a small guesthouse in Demachiyanagi, near the river. We considered a day trip to Nara but may skip it to keep the pace slow. Packing: light layers, a rain jacket, running shoes, and the camera with one lens. Budget check: accommodation is about half of what we planned to spend. Things to book later: the teamLab tickets in Tokyo and a cooking class in Kyoto. results.text: Nordwind phase 2 kickoff, notes exported from my meeting app. Attendees: Erik, two of their backend developers, their operations lead and me. We started with a recap of phase 1: the read-only Atlas API is live and the dispatch dashboard reads from it. Erik wants phase 2 to move order intake and driver assignment into the new TypeScript service. The operations lead walked through the current intake flow, which still depends on a nightly batch job. We agreed to keep the PHP monolith running in parallel for two weeks after the switch. Their developers asked for more integration tests around driver assignment; I'll write the first ones. Logging stays on their existing stack; we won't add a new vendor in this phase. There was a long discussion about how to migrate historical orders, and we parked it for a later session. Code reviews: every pull request needs one reviewer from their team and one from me. The cut-over to the new Atlas service is scheduled for Saturday 14 November 2026, overnight, when order volume is lowest. Rollback plan: switch the load balancer back to the monolith within 15 minutes if error rates double. We'll do a dry run of the cut-over in the staging environment the weekend before. Next steps: I send the phase 2 plan by Friday, they share production traffic numbers, and we meet again next Tuesday. Open question: whether the mobile driver app needs an update before the switch; their team will check. Everyone agreed the dashboard team should get a short demo
